scenes.topic: VOCA and FVPSA without the quarter-end scramble
scenes.vo: Priya, I put this short video together for you, about grant reporting at Riverbend Family Shelter.

scenes.headline: Two funders. One set of *numbers* rebuilt by hand.
lines: Services logged in one place, demographics in another
VOCA and FVPSA each want them their own way
scenes.vo: With VOCA and FVPSA both funding Riverbend, the same services get counted twice, by hand, in two different formats.
In NECX, every case is tagged to the grant that funds it, so services count toward the right grant from day one.
For VOCA, NECX builds the OVC PMT screen sheet from your logged services, and checks it against OVC's own rules before sign-off.
The FVPSA report fills in from the same records.
And Explain shows every record behind a number, and anything left out.

scenes.headline: Count it once. *Report* it everywhere.
items: Every case tagged to its grant
scenes.vo: Count each service once, check it before you certify, and explain every number.

scenes.question: Would it help to see last quarter's VOCA report built this way?

Marcus, this is a short video I made for you, about running the shelter side of Riverbend.

scenes.headline: Tonight's *bed count* lives on a whiteboard.
lines: The waitlist is a separate spreadsheet
scenes.vo: When the bed count lives on a whiteboard and the waitlist in a spreadsheet, intake is always guessing.
Here's NECX with Riverbend's name on it. Beds, hotline and what needs attention, the moment you sign in.
Every bed is available, occupied, reserved, or out of service, so tonight's count is the real count.
The waitlist sits right beside your beds.
And when a family needs a partner shelter, you choose exactly what goes with the referral.

scenes.headline: One live view of the *whole* shelter.
scenes.vo: One live bed board, the waitlist beside it, and referrals that share only what you choose.
